summary: The ExpenseBatch component models and manages batches of expenses associated with departments. It supports searching, adding, updating, and deleting expense batches through a set of stored procedures and entity classes.
purpose: To facilitate the creation, maintenance, and retrieval of expense batch records linked to departments, allowing for structured tracking and workflow management of expense processing.

fields.name: ID
fields.description: Unique identifier for the expense batch.

fields.name: BatchDescription
fields.description: A textual description of the batch.

fields.name: BatchDate
fields.description: The date the batch was created or is effective.

fields.name: StatusCodeID
fields.description: ID referencing the batch's workflow status.

fields.name: StatusCode
fields.description: The code representing the batch status.

fields.name: StatusDescription
fields.description: The description of the batch's status.

fields.name: ClosedDate
fields.description: Indicates when the batch was closed, if applicable.

fields.name: BatchNumberFormatted
fields.description: A formatted string combining the batch ID and its status description.

workflows.name: Search Expense Batches
steps: User initiates search by department ID.
System queries database for all batches for the given department in the last year.
Each result row is mapped to an ExpenseBatch object, with key fields populated.
BatchNumberFormatted is composed by combining the batch ID and status description.

workflows.name: Retrieve Expense Batch By ID
steps: User or system provides an ExpenseBatch ID.
System calls 'ExpenseBatchSearchID' stored procedure with the provided ID.
System populates all entity fields from returned data, including handling alternate language fields for descriptions if needed.

workflows.name: Add Expense Batch
steps: User provides department ID, batch description, and batch date.
System sets stored procedure to 'ExpenseBatchAdd' and passes parameters, including current session.
Database inserts the record and returns the new batch ID.

workflows.name: Update Expense Batch
steps: User supplies batch ID and updated field values.
System sets stored procedure to 'ExpenseBatchUpdate' and passes all parameters.

workflows.name: Delete Expense Batch
steps: System sets stored procedure to 'ExpenseBatchDelete' and passes ID.

business_rules: BatchNumberFormatted is created as a string concatenating batch ID and status description.
Status descriptions are language-dependent; alternate language fields may be used based on session settings.
validations: Batch ID must be a valid int (for update/delete).
Department ID must be provided (for add/search).
BatchDate must be a valid DateTime (for add/update).
conditions: If session is using alternate language fields, use StatusDescriptionAlt; otherwise, use StatusDescription.
system_behavior: All CRUD operations are routed via stored procedures.
All database connections are managed through session-based abstractions.
dependencies: ExpenseBatch stored procedures: ExpenseBatchSearch, ExpenseBatchSearchID, ExpenseBatchAdd, ExpenseBatchUpdate, ExpenseBatchDelete.
exceptions: If result set is empty, return empty objects/lists.
If input parameters are invalid, stored procedures may fail or return no result.
content_gaps: No explicit error handling logic is described.
No authorization or authentication checks are mentioned.
No detailed description of all possible status codes or their meanings.
